generic_name: Dextroamphetamine Saccharate, Amphetamine Aspartate Monohydrate, Dextroamphetamine Sulfate, Amphetamine Sulfate
purpose: This medication is used to treat Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in children and adults. It helps improve focus, attention, and control of behavior. It is also sometimes used to treat a sleep disorder called narcolepsy.
how_it_works: This medicine works by increasing the levels of certain natural chemicals in your brain, especially dopamine and norepinephrine. Think of it like turning up the volume on the parts of your brain that help you pay attention and stay in control. This helps calm the overactive signals in the brain that make focusing difficult for people with ADHD.
common_side_effects: Decreased appetite or not feeling hungry, trouble sleeping especially if taken late in the day, dry mouth, headache, stomach upset or nausea, increased heart rate, feeling anxious or nervous, and irritability or mood changes.
warnings: This medication can be habit-forming, so take it exactly as prescribed and never share it with others. Tell your doctor if you have heart problems, high blood pressure, a history of mental health issues, or a family history of heart disease. Avoid taking it in the afternoon or evening as it can cause insomnia. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor. It should not be taken with or within 14 days of taking an MAO inhibitor antidepressant as this can cause a dangerous reaction.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 6 and older, the immediate-release tablet is usually started at a low dose of 5 mg once or twice daily and slowly increased as needed. The extended-release capsule (XR) is typically taken once in the morning. Your doctor will find the right dose for you, usually no higher than 40 mg per day for ADHD. Always take it exactly as your doctor tells you.
